column1: # HDIC is an abbreviation of the Integrated Database of Hanzi Dictionaries in Early Japan
# KRM: Database of the Kanchi-in Manuscript of Ruijū Myōgishō
# Ruiju myogishō 類聚名義抄, Kanchi-in manuscript 観智院本, reorganized edition 改編本.
# anonymous Buddhist monk, the latter half of the 12th century.
# Copyright (c) 2025-2026 HDIC project, IKEDA Shoju (Chair, Professor Emeritus, Hokkaido University)
# Data License Information and Access Rights
# Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC BY-SA 4.0)
# The Phonetic Glosses in the Kanchi-in manuscript of the Ruiju Myōgishō include Fanqie spellings (反切), Similar sound notes (類音注, ruion-chū), and Kana glosses (仮名注, kana-chū).
# These are often accompanied by Tone marks (声点, shōten).

# As a database for Sino-Japanese pronunciations, the "Database of Historical Sino-Japanese Readings" (abbreviated as DHSJR), developed by Professor Katō Taitsuru and others, offers exceptionally rich content.
# Its specifications are also publicly available in detail.
# Accordingly, as part of the HDIC project, we have decided to release data in accordance with the DHSJR specifications.
# The DHSJR defines a data structure with 23 column names.

# To facilitate linkage with the Ruiju Myōgishō data included in HDIC, it is necessary for HDIC to assign unique column names to its own data files and to establish Primary Keys and Foreign Keys for interoperability between HDIC's internal data files.
# For this purpose, pronunciation_id (音注ID) has been set as the Primary Key, and definition_seq_id (注文ID) as the Foreign Key.
# Since the Ruiju Myōgishō features diverse formats for its Phonetic Glosses, a classification field named annotation_format (音注型) has been established to categorize them.
# While DHSJR uses Japanese column names, HDIC employs English ones. Therefore, for data processing convenience within HDIC, English column names have been adopted.

column2: DHSJR unique ID for each single Hanzi (Chinese character) (integrated data only).
(This column is currently empty. The data will be added once the official IDs are finalized by the DHSJR project.)

ID for each Phonetic Gloss. This is derived from definition_seq_id by extracting only those elements where the type (from definition_type_name in krm_notes) is Phonetic Gloss. Suffixes 'b', 'c', 'd' are appended for variant forms.

An identifier for each component of the Definition (Original Glosses) or for the Headword itself within an Entry. It is formed by appending a sequential suffix (e.g., "_00" for the Headword, "_01", "_02" for subsequent elements) to the corresponding entry_id.
Sequential number of a Hanzi (Chinese character)'s appearance in the material.

column1: #                           Numbers 1–27978 correspond to the physical order of characters in the original manuscript.
#                           Numbers 30001 and above are assigned to records added after the initial encoding
#                           (e.g., annotation characters newly identified as requiring separate entries)
#                           and do not correspond to physical positions in the manuscript.

column2: Sequential number of a Chinese word's appearance in the material
Headword column for Hanzi (Chinese characters) with Phonetic Glosses
Hanzi (Chinese characters) that have Phonetic Glosses
Headword column of Chinese words containing Hanzi (Chinese characters) with Phonetic Glosses
Chinese words containing Hanzi (Chinese characters) with Phonetic Glosses
Entered when there is an alphabetic representation of the Chinese word
Indicates the word type when there are mixed-language words (e.g., hybrid Sino-Japanese words)
Position of the single Hanzi (Chinese character) within the Chinese word
Number of morae for the single Hanzi (Chinese character)
Tone marks for single Hanzi (Chinese characters), indicating Four Tones (平上去入), Six Tones (平平軽上去入軽入), and voicing (清濁).
Combination of Tone marks for Chinese words. Hanzi (Chinese characters) without Tone marks are represented by a full-width asterisk (＊).
Kana glosses (仮名注) for Hanzi (Chinese characters), including kana-based fanqie.
Combination of Kana glosses for Chinese words. Hanzi (Chinese characters) without Kana glosses are represented by a full-width asterisk (＊).
Fanqie spellings (反切) for single Hanzi (Chinese characters).
Similar sound notes (類音注) for single Hanzi (Chinese characters).
Pattern of combined phonetic information (e.g., Kana glosses, Fanqie spellings, Similar sound notes, Tone marks).
Fushi-hakase notations (melodic or intonational markings) attached to musical materials such as Shōmyō (Buddhist chant).
Location of single Hanzi (Chinese characters) and Chinese words within the material.
Matters to be noted regarding these phonetic elements.

column25: 「跪」は広韻「去委切」（上声紙韻渓母）、「渠委切」（上声紙韻群母）の二音あり、後者が上声全濁字。原文「渠鬼反…音詭又音危（平濁）」の三音を記載。反切の「渠鬼反」は上声尾韻群母、類音注の「詭」は「過委切」（上声紙韻見母）であり、広韻音に近似。「危」は「魚爲切」（平声支韻疑母）であり、この声調に合致。よって、広韻と別系統の音を記載したと見られる。

column25: 音注字。「危」は「魚爲切」（平声支韻疑母・次濁）。見出し字「跪」の廣韻音（上声紙韻）とは別系統の平声音を示す。

column25: 廣韻「土」は「他魯切」（上声姥韻透母）・「徒古切」（上声姥韻定母）の二音。類音注「音吐（平濁）ト」の音注字「吐」は廣韻に平声エントリなし（上声・去声のみ）。図書寮本に「宋云本音吐(上)、音杜」とあり、漢音系では上声が正音。観智院本の平濁声点は呉音系の音を示す可能性があり、上声全濁字の声調対応の分析対象としては除外する。
